Perfect! Now I can analyze the carbon shifts. According to the reference data:
- Aromatic C-H (Ar-H): 115-130 ppm
- Aromatic C (Ar-C): 130-150 ppm

Looking at my 13C NMR data:
- 135.80 ppm: This falls in the aromatic carbon range (130-150 ppm for Ar-C)
- 117.40 ppm: This falls in the aromatic C-H range (115-130 ppm for Ar-H)
- 70.50 ppm: This is in the R3C-O or alkyne region (not aromatic)
- 54.00 ppm: This is in the aliphatic region, possibly H3C-O or epoxide (not aromatic)
- 43.70 ppm: This is in the aliphatic region, R₂CH or RCH₂ (not aromatic)

So I have 2 aromatic carbons:
1. One at 135.80 ppm (aromatic quaternary or substituted carbon)
2. One at 117.40 ppm (aromatic C-H)

The count of aromatic carbons is 2.
</thought>
